claims.claim: Linux namespaces isolate views of global resources such as process IDs, mounts, networking, users, IPC and hostnames.
claims.kind: kernel behavior, API or project documentation
claims.notes: Namespace isolation is not by itself a complete security boundary.

claims.claim: cgroup v2 organizes processes hierarchically and exposes resource controllers through a unified hierarchy.
claims.kind: kernel behavior, API or project documentation
claims.notes: Available controllers and delegation depend on kernel configuration and hierarchy setup.

claims.claim: OverlayFS combines lower and upper layers into a merged filesystem view and uses copy-up behavior for modifications.
claims.kind: kernel behavior, API or project documentation
claims.notes: Exact copy-up and metadata behavior depends on mount options and kernel version.

claims.claim: Container isolation also depends on capabilities, seccomp, LSM policy and runtime configuration.
claims.kind: kernel behavior, API or project documentation
claims.notes: No single namespace configuration guarantees isolation from all host resources.
